title: 208. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Rational Inequalities Using Sign Charts
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a basic rational inequality by determining the sign of the quotient.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x-4}{x+3}>0\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=-3\) and \(x=4\). The value \(x=-3\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero. The quotient is positive when the numerator and denominator have the same sign. On \(x<-3\), both factors are negative, so the quotient is positive. On \(-3<x<4\), the factors have opposite signs, so the quotient is negative. On \(x>4\), both factors are positive, so the quotient is positive. Therefore the solution is \(x<-3\) or \(x>4\).
questions.hint: Find the values that make the numerator or denominator zero, then test the sign of the quotient on each interval.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality and include or exclude endpoints according to the domain.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x-3}{x+1}\le0\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\). The value \(x=-1\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero. The quotient is nonpositive when the numerator and denominator have opposite signs or when the numerator is zero. On \(-1<x<3\), the numerator is negative and the denominator is positive, so the quotient is negative. At \(x=3\), the quotient is \(0\), which satisfies the inequality. Therefore the solution is \(-1<x\le3\).
questions.hint: Determine where the quotient is negative, and check whether the zero of the numerator is allowed.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality by identifying intervals where the quotient is nonnegative.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x+2}{x-4}\ge0\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=-2\) and \(x=4\). The value \(x=4\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero. The quotient is nonnegative when the numerator and denominator have the same sign or when the numerator is zero. On \(x<-2\), both factors are negative, so the quotient is positive. On \(-2<x<4\), the factors have opposite signs, so the quotient is negative. On \(x>4\), both factors are positive, so the quotient is positive. At \(x=-2\), the quotient is \(0\). Therefore the solution is \(x\le-2\) or \(x>4\).
questions.hint: Use the critical values to divide the number line, then test the sign of the quotient on each interval.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a strict rational inequality and express the solution as an open interval.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x-1}{x-3}<0\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=1\) and \(x=3\). Both values are excluded because \(x=3\) makes the denominator zero and \(x=1\) makes the quotient zero, but the inequality is strict. The quotient is negative when the numerator and denominator have opposite signs. On \(1<x<3\), the numerator is positive and the denominator is negative, so the quotient is negative. Therefore the solution is \(1<x<3\).
questions.hint: Test the sign of the quotient between and outside the critical values, and exclude endpoints for a strict inequality.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality by first rewriting it as a single fraction.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x+3}{x-2}\ge1\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(1\) from both sides, then combine the terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{x+3}{x-2}-1 &\ge 0\\
\frac{x+3-(x-2)}{x-2}=\frac{5}{x-2} &\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]
Since the numerator \(5\) is positive, the quotient is nonnegative exactly when the denominator is positive. Thus \(x-2>0\), so \(x>2\). The value \(x=2\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero.
questions.hint: Bring all terms to one side and combine them into a single fraction before analyzing signs.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality by subtracting a constant and analyzing the sign of the resulting single fraction.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x-2}{x+1}>1\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(1\) from both sides, then combine the terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{x-2}{x+1}-1 &> 0\\
\frac{x-2-(x+1)}{x+1}=\frac{-3}{x+1} &> 0
\end{aligned}
\]
Since the numerator \(-3\) is negative, the quotient is positive exactly when the denominator is negative. Thus \(x+1<0\), so \(x<-1\). The value \(x=-1\) is excluded.
questions.hint: Rewrite the inequality as a single fraction, then determine where the quotient is positive.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality by subtracting a constant and using a sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x+1}{x-2}\le2\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(2\) from both sides, then combine the terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{x+1}{x-2}-2 &\le 0\\
\frac{x+1-2(x-2)}{x-2}=\frac{5-x}{x-2} &\le 0
\end{aligned}
\]
The critical values are \(x=2\) and \(x=5\). The value \(x=2\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero. On \(x<2\), the numerator \(5-x\) is positive and the denominator is negative, so the quotient is negative. On \(2<x<5\), both numerator and denominator are positive, so the quotient is positive. On \(x\ge5\), the quotient is nonpositive, and at \(x=5\) it equals \(0\). Therefore the solution is \(x<2\) or \(x\ge5\).
questions.hint: Subtract \(2\) and combine into one fraction, then test the sign on the intervals determined by the critical values.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality with a constant on the right by constructing a sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x-3}{x+2}\ge2\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(2\) from both sides, then combine the terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{x-3}{x+2}-2 &\ge 0\\
\frac{x-3-2(x+2)}{x+2}=\frac{-x-7}{x+2} &\ge 0
\end{aligned}
\]
The critical values are \(x=-7\) and \(x=-2\). The value \(x=-2\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero. The quotient is nonnegative when the numerator and denominator have the same sign or when the numerator is zero. At \(x=-7\), the quotient is \(0\). On \(-7<x<-2\), the numerator \(-x-7\) is negative and the denominator \(x+2\) is negative, so the quotient is positive. On \(x<-7\), the numerator is positive and the denominator is negative, so the quotient is negative; on \(x>-2\), the numerator is negative and the denominator is positive, so the quotient is negative. Therefore the solution is \(-7\le x<-2\).
questions.hint: Combine the expression into a single fraction, then analyze the signs of the numerator and denominator.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality by transforming it into a single fraction and interpreting the sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x+4}{x-1}<2\).
questions.explanation:
Subtract \(2\) from both sides, then combine the terms:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{x+4}{x-1}-2 &< 0\\
\frac{x+4-2(x-1)}{x-1}=\frac{6-x}{x-1} &< 0
\end{aligned}
\]
The critical values are \(x=1\) and \(x=6\). The value \(x=1\) is excluded because it makes the denominator zero, and \(x=6\) is excluded because the inequality is strict. On \(x<1\), the numerator \(6-x\) is positive and the denominator is negative, so the quotient is negative. On \(1<x<6\), both numerator and denominator are positive, so the quotient is positive. On \(x>6\), the numerator is negative and the denominator is positive, so the quotient is negative. Therefore the solution is \(x<1\) or \(x>6\).
questions.hint: Rewrite the inequality as a single fraction, then use a sign chart and respect strict inequality endpoints.

questions.concept: Solving rational inequalities using sign charts
questions.learningObjective: Solve a rational inequality with fractions on both sides by combining them into one quotient.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{x-1}{x+2}\le\frac{x-3}{x+4}\).
questions.explanation:
Bring all terms to the left side and combine:
\[
\frac{x-1}{x+2}-\frac{x-3}{x+4}\le0
\]
The common denominator is \((x+2)(x+4)\). The numerator is
\[
(x-1)(x+4)-(x-3)(x+2)=4x+2=2(2x+1)
\]
So the inequality becomes
\[
\frac{2(2x+1)}{(x+2)(x+4)}\le0
\]
The critical values are \(x=-4\), \(x=-2\), and \(x=-\frac{1}{2}\). The values \(x=-4\) and \(x=-2\) are excluded because they make a denominator zero. The quotient is nonpositive when the numerator and denominator have opposite signs or when the numerator is zero. Sign analysis gives \(x<-4\) or \(-2<x\le-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Combine the two fractions into one quotient, then determine the sign of the numerator and denominator on each interval.
